map.地膜覆盖计算器，求地膜用量、覆盖面积与覆盖率，辅助采购数量与铺设规划，减少浪费。: The mulch coverage calculator works out film usage, coverage area and coverage rate to help plan purchasing quantities and laying, reducing waste.
map.有效膜宽 = (膜宽 − 搭接量) ÷ 100 (m)；铺膜行数 = ⌊地块宽(: Effective film width = (film width - overlap) / 100 (m); film rows = floor(plot width (cm) / row spacing (cm)); coverage = covered area / plot area x 100%; film weight = length x film width (m) x thickness (m) x density 0.92 g/cm3
map.铺膜行数按地块宽度除以行距向下取整，与「地宽 ÷ 有效膜宽」取较大值以满足最小铺: Film rows are the floor of plot width divided by row spacing, taking the larger of that and "plot width / effective film width" to meet minimum laying needs; total film length = rows x plot length. Coverage area = total film length x effective film width, divided by plot area gives coverage. Film weight is converted from length x width x thickness at a PE density of about 0.92 g/cm3, for purchase quantity and cost estimation.
map.覆盖面积 = 畦长 × 畦宽 × 行数，扣减重叠与损耗。: Coverage area = bed length x bed width x number of rows, minus overlap and waste.
map.按膜宽与种植行距匹配减少浪费。: Match film width to planting row spacing to reduce waste.
map.用于地膜需求量与成本估算。: For estimating mulch film demand and cost.
map.：地块 10 畦、每畦长 50 m、膜宽 0.9 m，理论覆盖 = 10×50×: : plot with 10 beds, each 50 m long and film 0.9 m wide: theoretical coverage = 10 x 50 x 0.9 = 450 m2 = 0.675 mu. Adding 5% lap waste means about 0.71 mu equivalent of film actually needed (converted to length by roll width).
map.地膜越宽越省吗？: Is wider film always more economical?
map.宽膜减少接缝但边角浪费可能增。应按畦面宽选膜，使膜边入土压实即可，过宽反增成本与: Wider film reduces seams but may increase edge waste. Match film to bed width so the edges can be buried and compacted; excessive width only raises cost and recovery difficulty.
map.残膜怎么处理？: How to deal with film residue?
map.地膜易残留污染土壤，应推广加厚可回收膜或生物降解膜，收获后及时回收。本工具不解决: Mulch film easily leaves residue that pollutes soil, so promote thicker recyclable film or biodegradable film and recover it promptly after harvest. This tool does not solve recovery; it only computes usage.
